chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm, from Shihāb ibn ʿAbd Rabbih, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: O Shihāb, I like that when I perform the Maghrib salat (prayer), I see a star in the sky.

So the aspect of recommendation in this report is that a person should proceed calmly in his salat (prayer) and perform it with deliberation; for when he does that, his completion of it will coincide with the appearance of the stars.

It is also possible that this is specific to one who is in a place where he cannot determine the disappearance of the redness from the east, such as when he is between high walls or lofty mountains. Indeed, one whose condition is like this ought to take precaution in that by observing the stars; this indicates that.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation; an act being preferable rather than obligatory
key_terms.الْكَوَاكِبِ: the stars, used as an indicator for timing
key_terms.الْمَشْرِقِ: the east, from which the redness is observed
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the Maghrib salat (prayer), the sunset prayer
key_terms.تُؤَدَةٍ: deliberation and calmness in performing the act
key_terms.سُقُوطِ الْحُمْرَةِ: the disappearance of the redness, referring to the twilight glow
key_terms.كَوْكَبًا: a star, used here as a visible sign in the sky

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith in al-Istibṣār say about seeing a star when performing Maghrib salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report concerns the timing of Maghrib salat (prayer) and indicates a recommended practice related to observing the appearance of a star in the sky. It explains that this may reflect praying with calm deliberation, or serve as a practical sign for those unable to observe the disappearance of twilight due to their surroundings.
